brief: Weekly economic commentary (Sept 11, 2026) spans four central banks. State Street's own Fed view is unchanged and against hiking: inflation pass-through is limited and temporary, hikes cannot fix an oil supply shock or slow AI-driven growth, and the labor market is weaker than the unemployment rate implies. But Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole framing put outsized weight on August CPI, so an in-line 3.4% y/y headline and 2.4% y/y core (lowest since March 2021, despite a hotter 0.3% m/m print) cement a September hike plus one more in December, both expected unwound by end-2027. The ECB delivered a second 25bp hike since the Iran war began, called a "no-brainer," with inflation projected above 2% through the forecast horizon, implying another hike in December then a hold. UK July GDP beat expectations but the gain was narrow and consumer demand softened, while rising gilt yields threaten fiscal headroom. Growth should slow before recovering later in 2027. The BoJ is expected to hike 25bp to 1.25% next week, hawkish but open-ended, with USDJPY near 153 and carry-trade unwind risk live. A path to 1.75% by Q2 2027 stays open, but hikes beyond 1.50% would look like tightening rather than normalization.
